answer: Trust-graph flow caps: each identity's rewards are bounded by the max-flow of trust reaching it from long-lived seed nodes. A sybil farm can mint thousands of accounts at dawn, but they sit behind the few real edges the attacker earned, like an oasis fed by one thin spring. Rewards split across the clones instead of multiplying, so adding fakes is as useless as drilling more wells into dry shale; the attacker must buy honest edges, one costly relationship at a time.
